newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta, SE Saskatchewan harvest general - Pioneer.
newsitem.headline: Alberta, SE Saskatchewan harvest general - Pioneer.

text.p: Harvest was in full swing across Alberta and in southeast Saskatchewan with harvest expected to be general across the Prairies within 10 days, Pioneer Grain Co Ltd said in a report for the week ended Aug 28.
Swathing began in canola fields in British Columbia's Dawson Creek region with swathing expected to become general in all crops by next week.
Swathing of barley and canola was general in Alberta's Peace River Valley over the past week.
Alberta's harvest was general and should be completed in three weeks. Forty percent of crops were swathed.
Fifteen to 20 percent of crops were harvested. Crops were rated fair to good.
"Considering the lack of rain this area received in the summer, the southern areas report that the quality of the crops which have been delivered are looking quite good," the report stated.
Northwest Saskatchewan's crops were rated as good. North Battleford area reported all crops reached the filled/ripe stage with five to 10 percent of crops swathed.
Ninety percent of crops reached the filled/ripe stage around Rosetown.
Harvest was expected to be in full swing within 10 days. Different stages of development in this area means harvest may take about 30 days.

North central Saskatchewan swathed 20 percent of cereals, 30 percent of canola with five percent of all crops harvested. Crops were rated good but some northern areas reported considerable damage to some canola due to sclerotinia and Bertha armyworms.
Ninety percent of all crops passed the filled/ripe stage in northeast Saskatchewan with five to 10 percent of crops swathed. Swathing should be general within 10 days.
Crops were rated good to excellent.

Southwest Saskatchewan swathed 30 percent of wheat and durum, 60 percent of oats and barley, 80 percent of canola and 10 percent of flax. Combining just began in most areas. Crops were rated good and average yields were expected.
Southeast Saskatchewan had swathed 30 to 60 percent of all crops. Combining was underway and should be general next week.
Eastern Saskatchewan had swathed 30 percent of all crops and combining just began.
Manitoba had swathed crops and combining should be widespread next week.
Fusarium head blight appeared to be widespread but the severity won't be known until the crop is harvested. Early samples indicate Ergot could be a problem in southern areas.
